summary: Candidate cdd6ac7 adds and unit-tests an opt-in DSpark-style confidence head, strict declared-head weight loading, DFlash2 STS loading/application, and preserves the earlier dynamic scheduling/ragged verification work. Its focused CPU and shared ROCm kernel tests pass. It does not fully resolve the original feature request: no compatible DFlash2 checkpoint or live DFlash2 target/draft pair validates the assumed checkpoint schema or end-to-end semantics, mixed-workload throughput is unmeasured, and an adversarial finite STS value can overflow during float32 conversion and be silently accepted as infinity.

gpu_execution.evidence: One AMD Instinct MI355X, gfx950, ran the shared kernel parity suite: 1 test passed and 22 subtests passed. No compatible DFlash2 model weights were available for architecture-qualified execution.

remaining_counterexamples: A finite positive STS JSON value larger than float32 range (for example 1e308) passes the shared calibration validator, becomes infinity when DFlashWorkerV2 converts it to float32, and is accepted; the calibrated confidence at that position collapses to 0.5 instead of rejecting invalid runtime calibration.

A real compatible DFlash2 checkpoint with a trained survival head has not been loaded, so the candidate's assumed enable_confidence_head/DSparkConfidenceHead naming, tensor shapes, bias, dtype, and optional Markov schema remain unverified against an actual DFlash2 artifact.
Lossless end-to-end semantics remain unverified for a real DFlash2 target/draft pair across sampling, grammar, continuous batching, overlap relay, and live compact graph replay.
The expected mixed-quality concurrent-workload throughput benefit remains unmeasured in live DFlash2 serving.
remaining_limitations: No compatible DFlash2 target/draft weights or trained confidence-head checkpoint were supplied or cached.
The qualified tiny Llama fixture is not DFlash2 architecture-qualified and therefore was not used as semantic or throughput proof.
GPU evidence is limited to shared DSpark kernels on AMD gfx950, not CUDA graph replay on NVIDIA hardware and not live DFlash2 serving.
No native source changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
